about.headline: Hi, I’m Janice
about.body:
I studied logistics, but the work felt monotonous and I wasn’t sure what I wanted to do next. A book nudged me to pay attention to what I did well in everyday life. At the time, Excel was the skill people around me seemed to value—and I enjoyed using it.

That small clue led to dashboards, Power BI, VBA, process automation, and a growing curiosity about AI. Agentic AI and vibe coding gave me a way to turn ideas into working prototypes, even while I’m still improving my engineering foundations.

These days I’m exploring how analytics, automation, and AI can make everyday work better. I learn by building, documenting what I learn, and leaving each project a little clearer than I found it.

projects.title: Human Bingo
projects.summary: A phone-friendly team-building game that replaces paper cards with a little more fun.
projects.motivation: I needed a human bingo activity for a team-building session and wanted to avoid printing, handing out, and keeping paper cards.
projects.built: A mobile-first bingo app where people can find matching teammates, mark squares, and play together from their phones.
projects.contribution: I shaped the interaction, built the prototype end to end, and iterated on the experience with the help of AI coding tools.
projects.learned: My first vibe-coding project taught me how quickly a clear, small problem can become a useful working prototype—and where I still need to slow down and understand the underlying code.

projects.title: Pingly
projects.summary: A playful polling and appreciation app with music, custom avatars, and a gratitude board.
projects.motivation: I wanted to create my own polling experience, add music, and go beyond the question limits I had run into elsewhere.
projects.built: A redesigned polling experience with custom avatars, an original penguin mascot called Pingly, music generated with Suno, and a gratitude board with uploads.
projects.contribution: I redesigned the experience, created the visual direction and custom assets, extended the existing app, and guided AI coding tools through the changes.
projects.learned: Pingly taught me what it feels like to build on an existing codebase: understanding its database and architecture, making focused GitHub commits, and asking AI tools to work with the system that is already there. I built on the open-source project below rather than creating the original platform from scratch.
